explanation:
Choice B is correct. It's given that $f(x)=8(5)^{x}$ and $g(x)=f(x+3)$. Substituting $x+3$ for $x$ in $f(x)=8(5)^{x}$ gives $f(x+3)=8(5)^{x+3}$. Using the exponent addition property $a^{m+n}=a^{m}\cdot a^{n}$, this equation can be rewritten as $f(x+3)=8(5)^{x}(5)^{3}$. Evaluating $5^{3}=125$ gives $f(x+3)=8(5)^{x}(125)$, which can be rewritten as $f(x+3)=8(125)(5)^{x}$. Multiplying the constants yields $f(x+3)=1000(5)^{x}$. Since $g(x)=f(x+3)$, it follows that $g(x)=1000(5)^{x}$.

Why A is incorrect:

Choice A is incorrect. This may result from incorrectly multiplying the coefficient by the shift value instead of by the base raised to the shift power. The student may have calculated $8 \cdot 3 = 24$ instead of correctly computing $8 \cdot 5^{3} = 8 \cdot 125 = 1000$.
